key_insight: For autonomous ML engineering, a strong frontier model appears to matter more than an elaborate agent harness, with minimal-harness coding agents matching open-source state-of-the-art systems under the same time budget.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners, this suggests that investing in better model backbones may deliver higher returns than adding multi-agent orchestration, retrieval subagents, or other complex scaffolding for current MLE benchmarks.
method: Compared a minimal-harness coding agent with open-source state-of-the-art harnessed agents.
Held the backbone LLM and time budget constant to isolate harness effects.
Ran large-scale systematic ablation studies across harness machinery layers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, under equal time and the same frontier LLM backbone, open-source state-of-the-art harnesses showed no advantage over a single-session minimal-harness baseline.
watch_item: These conclusions are benchmark-dependent, so results may not transfer to tasks where long-horizon planning, tool diversity, or more complex environments make extra harness structure more valuable.
paper_title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
